chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Leaving Basie for Claude Hopkins and the Apollo fiasco
summary: Smith left the Reno Club for Claude Hopkins' band but was paid off in New York because he was not a New York musician.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I just want to get the time right. The sequence of events was when you went to New York in 1938 and left the Parker band, you were arranging and not playing much...
What was the order? Did you join Don Redman first and then Benny Carter?
Yes. I got with Don Redman first.
Because didn't you come back to Kansas City again before...?
You had two stints in New York.
So can you tell me what happened? You went to New York and you were arranging. Then did you come back to Kansas City and then go back to New York?
Or did you join one of these bands first?
No, no. When I came back to Kansas City the first time, I left Claude Hopkins' band. That's the band I was with. See, I left Basie down there in the Reno Club and went on off with Claude Hopkins.
But that didn't last long, did it.

We got to New York, and they gonna play... They had a date there at the Apollo Theatre, played a week there, and they said I couldn't make that because I wasn't a New York musician. So he just paid me off for the week and give me a week's salary for that week to play in the theatre that I would have played... He just paid me extra; paid me like I already had worked. So I got in my car... I had my wife with me. I got in my car, and drove, came all the way back to Omaha, Nebraska, and I linked up in Sioux City, Iowa, where I started arranging for Nat Towles.
